pages.text: $(italic)Creatures of ancient magic and wild nature. Faefolk trade physical resilience for devastating arcane power.$()$(br2)$(bold)Nature's Blessing$(): $(item)+30% magic damage$() and $(item)+10% mana regen$(), the highest racial magic bonus.$(br2)$(bold)Fae Swiftness$(): $(item)+10% movement speed$().$(br2)$(bold)Slow Fall$(): you drift on the wind and take less fall damage.

pages.title: Tradeoffs
pages.text: $(bold)Frail Strikes$(): $(warn)-30% melee damage$(); the fae body is unsuited to brute force.$(br2)$(bold)Fae Fragility$(): $(warn)-15% max HP$().$(br2)$(bold)Ethereal Form$(): $(warn)-50% armor toughness$() in any medium or heavy armor. Full robes (4/4 light pieces) bypass it.$(br2)$(bold)Either way you pay:$() robes cost you light armor's -20% generic armor, plate the toughness halving.

pages.title: Build Notes
pages.text: $(bold)Archmage$(): the best fit. A pure caster in full robes, and your +30% magic damage adds to Arcane Supremacy's.$(br2)$(bold)Battlemage$(): $(thing)offmeta but viable$(). The -30% melee malus hurts, but Arcane Cleave converts your spell power to bonus AD. You'll never out-DPS an Orc Battlemage in raw melee. Spell-fueled hits and Mana Shield do make you tankier than a pure mage.

pages.title: Build Notes, cont.
pages.text: $(bold)Avoid:$() Berserker, Vanguard and Paladin. The melee malus and HP loss make them strictly worse choices.
